note: Prompt-only scaffold for future benchmarking. No assertions/harness run yet (skill was built by-feel).

evals.prompt: I'm adding a feature where creating an Order should send a confirmation email in the background using River. Wire up the job args, worker, and the enqueue in my Postgres handler. Make sure a rolled-back order never sends an email.
evals.expected_output: Enqueues via InsertTx in the same pgx.Tx as the order write; SendEmailArgs carries the order ID not the whole object; worker re-fetches; idempotent send.

evals.prompt: I want to use River with SQLite in a small single-binary tool, and I'd like the River UI dashboard available too. How do I set up the client and run the UI in Docker?
evals.expected_output: riversqlite.New(db) with SetMaxOpenConns(1)+PollOnly; River UI embedded via riverui.NewHandler (standalone image is Postgres-only); Dockerfile with DB file as a volume.

evals.prompt: Our River jobs are sometimes running twice and double-charging customers. Why, and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains at-least-once delivery (not a bug); fix is idempotency — idempotency key from job.ID, check-then-act, or DB constraint. Does not suggest exactly-once is achievable.

evals.prompt: Add a periodic job that recomputes tenant rollup stats every 5 minutes, and make sure two enqueues of the same refresh collapse into one.
evals.expected_output: river.NewPeriodicJob with PeriodicInterval(5m) + RunOnStart; UniqueOpts{ByArgs:true}; notes periodic jobs are leader-only/in-memory.
